interfaces.interface_notes: For the 19Al alloy at 650 °C/1 h the α matrix had almost completely transformed to β-Mn, with fine BCC and FCC (Cu-rich) precipitates located between/within the β-Mn.
interfaces.phase_evolution: α → α + FCC Cu-rich phase → α-Mn + β-Mn + BCC phase → β-Mn + BCC phase + FCC Cu-rich phase

processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Ingots with nominal composition Fe-35Mn-19Al-5Cu (at.%) produced by melting high-purity (>99.9 %) raw materials in a vacuum induction furnace under an argon atmosphere.
Ingots were homogenized at 1200 °C for 24 h.
Homogenized ingots were hot-rolled into plates with a thickness of 4 mm.
Plates were cut into 10 × 5 × 2 mm³ samples using electrical discharge machining for Vickers hardness measurements and microstructure characterizations.
Samples solution treated at 1100 °C for 10 min under an argon atmosphere, followed by oil quenching (parent process proc_st-1100c-10min-oq).
Solution-treated samples were aged at 650 °C for 1 h, followed by water quenching. This aging treatment defines the sample state of interest.

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: Vickers hardness measured with HVS-1000 digital microhardness tester, load 9.8 N, dwell 15 s; each value is the average of 5 measurements.

phases_present.morphology: matrix phase (near-complete transformation product of α after 1 h at 650 °C)

structures.overall_structure: After aging the 19Al (Fe-35Mn-19Al-5Cu at.%) low-density steel at 650 °C for 1 h, the α matrix had almost completely transformed into β-Mn; numerous fine new precipitates were distributed within the β-Mn.

unmapped_findings: Nominal composition of the 19Al alloy is Fe-35Mn-19Al-5Cu (at.%, x = 19 for the series Fe-35Mn-xAl-5Cu); EDS-measured composition is Fe 41.6, Mn 34.8, Al 18.6, Cu 5.0 at.% (Table 1).
The 19Al alloy density measured by the Archimedes method is 6.66 g·cm⁻³ (b0017) — the lowest of the three alloys (15Al 6.85, 17Al 6.76 g·cm⁻³).

In the 19Al alloy the α→β-Mn transformation kinetics were slowed relative to the 15Al/17Al alloys by the higher Al content; at 650 °C (i.e. ≥600 °C) the α matrix had almost completely transformed into β-Mn after just 1 h of aging (b0053).

The optimal aging-temperature window for reaching ultra-high hardness in the 19Al alloy is ~575–625 °C (b0038); the 650 °C/1 h condition therefore lies slightly above this optimum, being part of the essentially time-independent ~801–811 HV plateau seen at 650 °C.
